messages:
maria: Quick summary: ran a mixed-quant bakeoff (FP8 / INT8 / AWQ / GPTQ) on the 13B conversational model with prefix cache + continuous batching enabled. Saw consistent ~0.9-1.5% EM drop for AWQ when prefix cache is turned on vs off. Strange because INT8/GPTQ stable.
aj: Can you share the exact config and perf/quality numbers?
maria: Uploaded results to the eval dashboard: https://internal/redwood/evals/1769456000 (private). Key bits: batcher=continuous, prefix_cache=on, cache_ttl=3600s, kv_layout=separate, beam=1.
lee: Do we know whether the AWQ variant changes KV shapes or has different attention kernel ordering? That could break cache key equality.
maria: I dug into the KV fingerprints — cache hits are ~12% lower on AWQ with same inputs. Also saw small drift in first-token logits when cache misfires.
sophia: Could be quantization-induced softmax / scaling differences causing early tokens to differ and then propagate. AWQ uses asymmetric scales per-head, which might change the initial hidden states subtly.
dmitri: Reproduced locally. With prefix_cache on: AWQ top-1 accuracy 78.3%. Prefix_cache off: 79.7%. INT8 stays ~79.6 both ways.
aj: Important question: are we saving cached keys in float32 or quantized form? If we store quantized KV and then do mixed-type matmuls, rounding could introduce mismatch.
maria: We store cache in fp16 currently for all variants to keep runtime stable. But AWQ kernels internally use int8-ish ops then dequantize — maybe numerical path differs.
sophia: Quick experiment idea: force AWQ runtime to do an identical dequant->fp16 path as INT8 (if possible) and compare. Also run a strict token-level diff on sequences where cache hit vs miss.
lee: I pushed a small patch to log first 16 dims of K/V pre- and post-quant for a sample set: 
```
# sample log
k_pre: [-0.012, 0.234, ...]
k_post: [-0.0117, 0.2339, ...]
```
Not huge but cumulative.
dmitri: Also noticed continuous batching reorders requests (for throughput). If ordering + tiny numeric differences cause different fused attention schedule, cache keys (which include position indices) might not align across workers.
aj: Good point — cache key is (model,seq_hash,position,kv_digest). If seq_hash computed from token ids only, reordering shouldn't matter, but position/scoped start index might. Are we normalizing start_pos consistently in batching path?
maria: There was a subtle bug in start_pos normalization for batched prefix merges — fixed in PR #4321 but only present in the dedicated runtime. The hosted runtime had a different codepath.
sophia: So we might have a combination: AWQ micro-numerics + start_pos mismatch under continuous batching produce cache misses and drift.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: canary rolled AWQ patch to stg cluster (rev awq-2026-03-12). Keep an eye on latency.
dmitri: After applying start_pos fix + forcing fp16 cache storage, AWQ accuracy with prefix_cache on improved to 79.5% (within noise of others). Still ~0.1% delta.
lee: That residual could be quantization model mismatch. Suggest we add a post-quant calibration pass (small eval set) to generate correction scales for prefix token embeddings.
aj: Also add unit test that compares per-token logits for a small seed across quant variants with cache on/off. Fail if delta > 1e-3 L2.
maria: Agreed. Action items: 1) apply start_pos normalization patch across runtimes (maria) 2) add fp16 cache canonicalization for all quant variants (lee) 3) run small-scale calibration on AWQ to reduce residual drift (sophia) 4) add CI diff test (aj). I'll open PRs and schedule a short rerun tomorrow morning.
sophia: I'll prepare the eval set and scripts.
ci-bot: CI queue: 3 jobs queued for awq-prefetch-tests, ETA ~12m.
maria: Thanks all. If anyone sees weird latency regressions after the patch ping here. :thumbsup:
